1 [Ἀντικοὺς haud aliud est atque Ἀντίοχος (cf. supra, p. 66), quod nomen arabice
Antikus scriptum erat. Στόχος quid significet nescio, nisi forte ex Στωϊκός cor-
ruptum sit. Mirum est Ptolemaei tetrabiblum non commemorari. — F. C.]
sections.en:
1 [Ἀντικοὺς ('Antikous') is nothing other than Ἀντίοχος ('Antiochus') (cf. above, p. 66), which name in Arabic
was written Antikus. What Στόχος ('Stochos') means I do not know, unless perhaps it is corrupted from Στωϊκός ('Stoic').
It is surprising that Ptolemy's Tetrabiblos is not mentioned. — F. C.]

summary.headline: Astrological Books and Authorities
summary.text: Astrological bibliography attributed to Hermes, Plato, Dorotheus, Democritus, Aristotle, Antikous, Valens, Erasistratus, Stochos, and the Persians, listing their books by subject: nativities, interrogations, zodiacal degrees, calculations, conjunctions, eclipses, fardars, and fortunes. The author says he compiled a concise work from Ptolemy, Hermes, and earlier authorities, including two Persian books transmitted to India.
